proposals.what_changes: Replaces the frozen outlier_mad program with a hampel_filter, which removes local spikes via a rolling window median rather than global MAD scaling, targeting the same class of extreme local deviations but with a mechanism that may reduce single-series harm compared to MAD on the series that were damaged.

proposals.expected_change: Changes treatment on series that have both local outliers and level-excursion signals; the additional step is intended to reduce harm on series where MAD alone overcorrected, by removing any residual level shift and thus improving aggregate gain over the current single-step program.

proposals.what_changes: Restrict treatment to series with a pronounced level excursion, which are the clear outlier cases the MAD program has consistently helped (T140, T144, T146, T150, T152, T156, T158 at unit 10), while excluding borderline or non-level series that drive the recurring harmed_fraction and single_series_harm failures.
proposals.expected_change: Keeps the eight series that gained at unit 10, preserves the zero-harm profile that passed all risk lines there, and raises the treated count back above the coverage floor, avoiding the overcorrection that damaged borderline series under the current broad local-robust-z scope.

proposals.what_changes: Replace the single MAD step with a two-step correction that first applies IQR outlier adjustment and then MAD adjustment; the IQR step is intended to be more conservative than MAD alone, reducing the magnitude of overcorrection on borderline series while still flagging the same clear peaks.
proposals.expected_change: Lowers worst_single_series_harm and harmed_fraction on the currently treated series because the first pass caps the extreme deviations that the MAD-only program over-removes, while retaining positive aggregate gain on the clear outlier series that have consistently gained; coverage should stay above the floor because the same outlier regions are still adjusted.

proposals.what_changes: Replaces the frozen MAD correction with a median denoiser that never removes values, only suppresses noise, so it should retain the positive aggregate gain seen on clear outlier series while avoiding the extreme overcorrections that repeatedly drove harmed_fraction and single_series_harm past their limits.
proposals.expected_change: Median-based denoising keeps a smooth baseline for treated series; for outlier peaks it reduces their amplitude without deleting points, so affected series stay close to their original forecast support and should show lower worst-case harm than MAD, winsorize, or hampel while still improving aggregate gain on strong-peak series.

proposals.what_changes: Replaces MAD correction with IQR-based outlier adjustment, giving the treated series a more conservative, distribution-tolerant correction than the current MAD scope and prior candidate programs that all failed the harm lines.
proposals.expected_change: For series with strong local outliers, IQR trimming caps extreme deviations at moderate quantile bounds instead of the more aggressive MAD removal, so it should maintain positive gain on the strong-peak series that cleared the coverage floor in earlier replays while keeping single-series harm from spiking above the failure threshold.

actual_cost.counting: every physical fit, including the ones spent inside a call that then raised; no allowance carried over

ledgers.course_fits_cover: the delayed gate and the evaluation face
ledgers.support_fits_note: Support probe fits, counted only where the evaluator reported them; probes that reported none are counted as unrecorded rather than as zero.  Courses run before this counter existed have no Support line at all and their Support cost stays a derivation, not a reading
ledgers.baseline_note: the reference model, shared by every arm on a unit because it is cached per (executor, origin).  COMPLETED executions and cache hits are counted; they are not folded into support_fits and not priced, because the injected evaluator reports no fit count and charging a shared model is an open protocol question
ledgers.baseline_evaluations_is_not_a_fit_total: it counts completed reference evaluations, one per (executor, origin).  What each one costs the Consumer is not reported by the injected evaluator, so this line must not be read as, or added to, a total of Consumer fits
ledgers.unmeasured_cost_note: an evaluation that raised inside the Consumer had already spent an unrecoverable amount: scoped_evaluate reports consumer_fits only on a normal return.  Those are counted here as unmeasured rather than added to any total as zero
ledgers.why_no_llm_prompt_cache: wiring CachedAgentBackend would change what the arms are charged for and how their proposals diverge; it is not enabled for HEC-1 and its absence is recorded rather than left as a zero that looks like a miss rate

code_state.why: historical behaviour may only be explained with the code that produced it; where HEAD differs the current file is not used
